newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks climb back into black by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks climb back into black by close.

text.p: A mixed Australian share market muddled its way to a firmer close on Friday as Dow-inspired strength in the industrials managed to overcome a resources sector weakened by soft precious and base metals prices.
Option exercises following Thursday's January series expiry inflated otherwise modest turnovers.
The All Ordinaries index added 6.0 points to 2,423.7.

"Commodities, especially gold, kept a large portion of the market down with people still wary," said dealer Peter Struk of Sydney-based brokerage, Reynolds and Co, adding that the impressive-looking volumes belied a reasonably slow day.
"It was large turnover due to options exercises but people really weren't interested today overall," he said.

Individual features came from outside the leaders. In the resources, Cultus Petroleum shares starred, leaping 31 percent to A$1.90 (US$1.45) after the company reported oil and gas shows from its Cornea wells offshore Western Australia.

In the industrials, biotechnology group Progen Industries extended its strong gains from Thursday when it announced encouraging results from animal tests of its anti-cancer compound. Its shares closed 18 percent higher at A$1.09.
The half yearly results continue to trickle in with two major base metals miners turning in their reports.
Shares in MIM Holdings shares ended a cent higher at A$1.75 after it posted a net loss of A$12 million for the six months to December 31, compared to a profit of A$58.9 million previously.
North Ltd shares closed two cents higher at A$3.94 after increasing first half net profit by 50 percent to A$50 million.

Junior explorer Carnarvon Petroleum shares topped turnover by volume with 52.9 million shares traded, closing steady at 2.5 cents. The bulk of the activity was in one line of 49.96 million shares crossed at 2.2 cents, with brokers saying 11.29 percent shareholder Devex looked likely to have sold its stake.
Falls shaded rises by the barest of margins, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
